title: Robichaux and Claiborne Williams bands compared
summary: He describes Robichaux's orchestra and Williams's band as classical dance music, with simple two-part orchestrations.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Seven. In regard to Robichaud, you said they played nice dance music. Did they usually just read music and play arrangements sort of or what?

Well, you know, just like the straight orchestration. They didn't have no more than two parts to it, you know, the first and second parts. Yeah. They didn't have no arrangements. Of course, the special arrangement thing didn't start after World War I.
No, I guess not. How would Robichaud's band compare with the Claiborne Williams band? Was it the same type of music?
The same type of music, yes, the classical.
Did Claiborne Williams ever play anything like blues or anything in their ear?
Just on a request, something like that to play some of these people.
They did know some of those.

Well, it's a good jazz band, good swing band, you know, but classical music, you know, at that time how they had the classical parts. It wasn't rough. Claiborne and neither was Robichaud. They didn't have no rough band. It was good music, good swing. But you know, they had some rock bottoms. It's five pieces. It's like piano, drum, band, cornet, maybe a trombone. You know, five pieces. Yes. That could make a plenty of noise.
